expectations.text: A canonical model file exists separate from the generated JSON Schema
expectations.evidence: with_skill/outputs/datamodel/model.yaml is the canonical model; JSON Schema generated separately at datamodel/exports/0.1.0/airquality.schema.json (response.md: '`model.yaml`: the canonical model').

expectations.text: Position is modelled as a value type/datatype without its own identity
expectations.evidence: model.yaml puts Position under `datatypes:` (not `classes:`), no identifier; response.md table: 'Position | A value type with lat, lon and optional altitude | n/a'.

expectations.text: Pollutant is modelled as an extensible or externally governed code list, not a closed enum or an undocumented plain string
expectations.evidence: model.yaml enumerations.Pollutant: 'extensible: true', 'authority: http://dd.eionet.europa.eu/vocabulary/aq/pollutant'; JSON Schema $defs/Pollutant is type string with examples (open). D-006 'Pollutant and unit as extensible code lists'.

expectations.text: The station kind is modelled as a closed enumeration with traffic, industrial and background
expectations.evidence: model.yaml enumerations.StationKind: 'extensible: false', values traffic/industrial/background; JSON Schema $defs/StationKind enum ['traffic','industrial','background'].

expectations.text: The meaning of the integer validity and verification codes is flagged as ambiguous
expectations.evidence: response.md item 2: '`validity` and `verification` are bare `xs:int`. The XSD gives no list of values and no meaning for them.' Q-005 blocking: 'Meaning of the validity and verification integers'.

expectations.text: The missing coordinate reference system for lat/lon is flagged
expectations.evidence: response.md item 8: 'The coordinate system, the altitude unit and the lat/lon ranges are not specified (A-005...)'; A-005 'lat/lon are WGS 84 (EPSG:4326)' assumed.

expectations.text: Identifier issues are flagged (xs:ID values only unique within one document, and/or overlap of id and stationCode)
expectations.evidence: response.md item 1: 'Identifiers are only valid inside one file... They only have to be unique within a single XML document'; D-005 treats station @id as document-local vs stationCode as key; Q-002.

expectations.text: The observation volume is estimated at roughly 21 million per year (400 x 6 x 24 x 365) and recorded
expectations.evidence: model.yaml Observation.nfr.volume: '≈ 57,600/day ≈ 21 M/year (400 stations × 6 pollutants × 24)'; growth '+21 M/year'; response table '~21 M/year'.

expectations.text: The high observation volume leads to an API design note (e.g. observations as a separate, paginated resource rather than nested in station documents)
expectations.evidence: decisions.md D-008: REST read resources '/sampling-points/{id}/observations?from=&to=' 'with observations paginated / time-windowed rather than embedded'; ObservationCollection nfr notes 'Too large as a single API response'.

expectations.text: The generated JSON Schema is a valid JSON Schema and allows null for the observation value
expectations.evidence: Ran python -I jsonschema: Draft202012Validator.check_schema OK on airquality.schema.json; $defs/Observation.value = anyOf [number, null]; an Observation with value null validates with 0 errors; examples/delivery.json validates with 0 errors. (Note: value is not in 'required', so absence is also allowed — D-009 documents this.)

suggestions.assertion: The observation volume is estimated at roughly 21 million per year (400 x 6 x 24 x 365) and recorded
suggestions.reason: Both runs pass trivially once they do 400x6x24x365; consider requiring the estimate be recorded in the canonical model itself (e.g. an NFR/volume field), which discriminates between 'mentioned in prose' and 'recorded in the model'.

suggestions.assertion: The generated JSON Schema is a valid JSON Schema and allows null for the observation value
suggestions.reason: Weakly discriminating: any generator that maps nillable to null passes. Consider also checking that a sample delivery instance validates and that value stays required (with_skill made value optional, so absent and null are equivalent — a real semantic change from the XSD that no assertion catches).

suggestions.assertion: Position is modelled as a value type/datatype without its own identity
suggestions.reason: Grading depends on model vocabulary; a run without a datatype concept (without_skill put Position under classes with no key) is ambiguous. State what counts as evidence (separate datatype section, or explicit 'no identity' statement).
No assertion checks XSD round-trip compatibility (generated XSD accepting what 2.1 accepts), which was an explicit user goal; both runs claim it, which could be verified with lxml.

eval_feedback.overall: Most assertions are flag-presence checks that a competent run passes regardless of skill; the discriminating ones are Position-as-datatype and Pollutant-as-extensible-code-list.
